answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism that requires each identity to secure unique sponsorship from established agents on a knoll. To participate, identities must bid for a limited number of slots, with the cost starting at 100 tokens and rising by 50 tokens for each new bidder. This mechanism reaches its nadir when the costs escalate beyond 1,000 tokens per slot, effectively walling off potential. An attacker might find themselves spending over 10,000 tokens, like trying to scale a steep mountain while burdened by a quill-stuffed backpack.
